ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
During the ripening process of banana fruit, the stored substances in the fruit are continuously metabolized and transformed, and the banana gradually becomes sweet. In Figure A, the two curves I and II respectively indicate the changing trends of the contents of two substances during the ripening process of banana fruit. Please answer:
Take equal amounts of banana pulp ripened to day X and day Y, respectively add equal amounts of distilled water to make extracts. Then add 5 mL of the extract from day X to each of test tubes a and b, and add 5 mL of the extract from day Y to each of test tubes c and d, as shown in Figure B. After adding equal amounts of iodine solution to test tubes a and c respectively, tube a turns blue. Which curve in Figure A indicates the changing trend of starch content?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The horizontal axis of Figure A is ripening time, marking day X and day Y; the vertical axis is the contents of two substances. Curve I gradually decreases as ripening time increases, with a relatively high content on day X and a relatively low content by day Y; curve II gradually increases as ripening time increases. In Figure B, test tubes a and b are added with the extract from day X, and test tubes c and d are added with the extract from day Y; above test tubes a and c it is labeled that iodine solution is added. Reasoning: The question stem states that tube a turns blue after iodine solution is added, and starch turns blue when it encounters iodine solution, indicating that the banana extract on day X contains relatively more starch. During the ripening process of bananas, they gradually become sweet, indicating that stored substances such as starch will be transformed, and the starch content should decrease as ripening time increases. Therefore, in Figure A, the one indicating the changing trend of starch content is the decreasing curve I.
